author: Zach Tuggle
title: Pools and cooling centers open during extreme heat in Richland County - NewsBreak
text:
By Zach Tuggle ,
1 days ago Swimming pools and cooling centers are helping people stay safe during Richland County's extreme heat warning.
The heat advisory will last until 8 p.m. July 2, according to Richland County EMA Director Sarah Potes.
Daytime highs this week will climb into the 90s with heat indexes of 100 degrees.
"As temperatures soar, staying cool is a matter of safety," Potes said.
More: Richland County could set new record high temperature with heat dome
Cooling centers in Richland County Several buildings in Richland County are open to shelter people from the heat.
Mansfield Richland County Public Library branches throughout the region will welcome guests all week. Local branch hours are available at mrcpl.org .
The Ontario Center, formerly known as the Richland Mall, is open 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. through July 3, then 11 a.m. to 4 p.m. July 4.
In Shelby, Marvin Memorial Library will be open 9 a.m. to 8 p.m. every day this week.
Shelby also will open a temporary cooling center at 5 Water St. 10 a.m. to 4 p.m. June 30 to July 2.
The Lexington Senior Depot, known as the Lexington Senior Civic Center, will be open as a cooling center 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. through July 2.
Area swimming pools are open Several swimming pools and splash pads in the area will help families stay cool this week.
The Heise Park Pool at 5 Heise Park Ln. in Galion will be free to the public 1 p.m. to 7 p.m. June 30 through July 2.
Galion's splash pad at East Park also is free every day of the summer.
Ontario has a free splash pad at Marshall Park.
The Mansfield Fire Department will be at Liberty Park in Mansfield 12-2 p.m. July 2 with hoses to create a temporary splash pad, free for local children.
The public pools in Shelby and Plymouth will be open all week, but regular admission still applies.
"There are numerous private pools in the area that many offer admission to the public for a fee," Potes said.
Private pools open for business include Walnut Hill, Clear Fork in Lexington, Shelly Acres, Lakewood, Woodland and the YMCA in Mansfield and Shelby.
Contact Zach Tuggle at 419-564-3508. Follow him on X at @zachtuggle.
This article originally appeared on Mansfield News Journal: Pools and cooling centers open during extreme heat in Richland County
